title: Dublin City Council extends its ban on street bin bags to residential Dublin 7
question: How will Dublin 7 residents react to this over the first two weeks, which groups will push back and why, and is Dublin City Council likely to keep, change or reverse the decision?

objections.text: Small terraced houses have no room for wheelie bins, which would sit on the street all week.
Switching to bin plans will raise household costs.
Residents were not consulted before the decision.
Private collectors control the options; a single area-wide collector is needed first.

backdown.summary: Start pushed from July to August, then to October with a consultation, then suspended with no date on 30 Sep 2026 after most consultation respondents opposed it. The council still intends to remove the derogation eventually.

pushback_groups: local Labour TD and Labour councillors
notes: CONTROL CASE (known_to_model: true): announced 7 May 2026, before the June 2026 cutoff, though the first press-documented pushback (15 June public meeting) is close to the cutoff and the suspension is after it. Backdown is partial: an indefinite suspension, not a formal repeal. Note the two-week window is weak here because organised protest started about five weeks after the first report.
